info.title: Symplast Financials Public API
info.description:
Authenticated, cursor-paged public read surface for financial data: payments, invoices, estimates, credit notes, gift cards, memberships and the catalog.

**Authentication.** Send a bearer token from the Symplast developer portal. The tenant is taken from the token; there is no tenant parameter. A missing or invalid token is 401, and a token without the scope a path requires is 403 with the required scope named in the body.

**Paging.** Every collection returns `data`, `hasMore` and `next`. Follow `next` verbatim and stop when `hasMore` is false; do not construct a cursor. A cursor is bound to the filters it was issued under, so changing a filter and replaying an old cursor is rejected rather than silently resumed. `pageSize` is a request, not a guarantee.

**Reading changes.** Collections are change feeds, ordered oldest change first, so a consumer can poll for what moved. Pass `updatedSince` (an inclusive ISO-8601 instant) and read `modifiedDateUtc` off each record to checkpoint. `modifiedDateUtc` is never null: for a record never edited it equals `createdUtcDate`. Deleted, void and cancelled records stay in the feed with their status, so a consumer can correct figures it already holds; filter them out by status if you do not want them.

**Errors** are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a stable `code` to match on.

**Reference data.** A tenant reference collection — brands, categories, item types, occasions, payment modes, payment and discount reasons — is a FULL read, not a change feed: the tables carry no timestamp, so there is no `updatedSince` and a consumer keeping a local copy re-reads the whole collection. Rows the practice has removed are included with `isDeleted: true`, because historical records still reference them; filter on that flag for what is currently selectable. A status vocabulary is contract metadata rather than tenant data: it arrives complete and unpaged, is identical for every tenant, and never includes the `Unknown` sentinel, which exists only to absorb a stored value from outside the contract on the way out.

**Money** fields are authoritative as published; do not recompute a total from the other fields.

**Free-text fields may contain patient information.** Where a field is described as operator free text, treat it as PHI: do not log it, index it, or use it as a cache key.

get.description: Every payment mode configured for the tenant, ordered by `id`. Group and compare on `paymentType`, since the name is practice-renamable and the id is tenant-local.
Every payment reason configured for the tenant, ordered by `id`.
Every discount reason configured for the tenant, ordered by `id`.
Every gift card occasion configured for the tenant, ordered by `id`. An id of 0 is the platform-seeded `Other` occasion rather than a not-set sentinel.
Every brand configured for the tenant, ordered by `id`. Additive to the inline `brand` object on an item.

Every flat item category configured for the tenant, ordered by `id`. A separate table from the hierarchical categories on `/v1/financials/item-hierarchical-categories`, with no parent and no delete flag.

Every hierarchical item category configured for the tenant, ordered by `id` and flat rather than nested, so build the tree client-side from `id` and `parentId`. Ordering is by id rather than tree position, so a child can arrive on an earlier page than its parent. `parentId` may name a category whose own `isDeleted` is true, so resolve it against this same collection including deleted rows.
Every item type configured for the tenant, ordered by `id`. Additive to the inline `itemType` object on an item.

A page of the tenant's estimates, each with its line items inline. Filters: `updatedSince`, `patientId`, `status` (repeatable, values from `/v1/financials/estimate-statuses`), and the inclusive `effectiveDateFrom` / `effectiveDateTo` range over `effectiveDate`. Rejected, cancelled, deleted and expired estimates are all returned, and a cloned estimate is an independent row with no link to its original, so a naive conversion rate double-counts the opportunity.
One estimate with its line items inline, the same payload the collection returns. An id belonging to another tenant answers 404 rather than 403.

A page of the tenant's invoices, each with its line items inline. Filters: `updatedSince`, `patientId`, `status` (repeatable, values from `/v1/financials/invoice-statuses`), and the inclusive `effectiveDateFrom` / `effectiveDateTo` range over `effectiveDate`. `amount` and `balanceDue` are authoritative, and `paidAmount` is `amount - balanceDue` from the invoice's own balance rather than a reconciliation against payments — the field notes on the schema carry the rest.
One invoice with its line items inline, the same payload the collection returns. An id belonging to another tenant answers 404 rather than 403.

A page of the tenant's credit notes, each with its line items inline. Filters: `updatedSince`, `patientId`, `status` (repeatable, values from `/v1/financials/credit-note-statuses`), and the inclusive `effectiveDateFrom` / `effectiveDateTo` range over `effectiveDate`. No tax field is published and its absence is not an implicit zero, `patientId` may be null, and `appliedAsPaymentAmount + refundedAmount + balance == amount` reading each null as zero.
One credit note with its line items inline, the same payload the collection returns. An id belonging to another tenant answers 404 rather than 403.

A page of the tenant's payments. Filters: `updatedSince`, `patientId`, `status` (repeatable, values from `/v1/financials/payment-statuses`), and the inclusive `paymentDateFrom` / `paymentDateTo` range over `paymentDate`. `amount` is unsigned so direction comes from `isRefund`, `paymentMode.paymentType` is the only classification comparable across tenants, and a null `patientId` is an insurance payment whose payer this contract does not publish.
One payment by id. An id belonging to another tenant answers 404 rather than 403.

A page of the tenant's membership programmes. Filters: `updatedSince` and `status`, which accepts the values `/v1/financials/membership-program-statuses` returns. Deletion here is a hard delete, so a removed programme simply stops appearing and cannot be detected incrementally — reconcile against a full unfiltered page if you must notice removals.

One membership programme by id. An id belonging to another tenant answers 404 rather than 403, and so does one that was hard-deleted, which is why a membership can name a programme this endpoint cannot return.

A page of the tenant's patient memberships. Filters: `updatedSince`, `patientId`, `status` (repeatable, values from `/v1/financials/membership-statuses`), and the inclusive `startDateFrom` / `startDateTo` range over `startDate`. `status` is derived and `Active` includes a membership that has not started yet, while `Past` is reserved and never returned because supersession cannot be derived from a single row.
One patient membership by id. An id belonging to another tenant answers 404 rather than 403.

A page of the tenant's gift cards. Filters: `updatedSince`, `status` (repeatable, values from `/v1/financials/gift-card-statuses`), and the inclusive `issuedDateFrom` / `issuedDateTo` range over `issuedDate`. `cardNumber` is always masked, `value` is the remaining balance while `maxValue` is the face value and a null there is not zero, and `description` is operator free text.
One gift card by id. An id belonging to another tenant answers 404 rather than 403.

A page of the tenant's catalog items, which are global to the tenant. Filters: `updatedSince`, `isForSale`, and the inclusive `createdFrom` / `createdTo` range over the calendar date of `createdUtcDate`. `isForSale`, `status` and `isDeleted` are three independent flags rather than one active state, and `flatPrice` is the global list price that a per-location price, a quantity tier or a document discount all override.
One catalog item by id. An id belonging to another tenant answers 404 rather than 403.

A page of the tenant's item groups, each a named bundle of catalog items with its members inline in `details[]`. Filters: `updatedSince` and `isActive`. No money amount and no `isForSale` is published, because both would depend on a location, a price schedule and a per-member discount kind that this contract does not carry.
One item group with its members inline, the same payload the collection returns. An id belonging to another tenant answers 404 rather than 403.
Every value a invoice's `status` field can carry, and every value its `status` filter accepts.
Every value a credit note's `status` field can carry, and every value its `status` filter accepts.
Every value a estimate's `status` field can carry, and every value its `status` filter accepts.

Every value a gift card's `status` field can carry, and every value its `status` filter accepts.

One merged field: `Draft` and `Deleted` are stored and take precedence, while `Expired` and `Redeemed` are derived on read.

Every value a membership's `status` field can carry, and every value its `status` filter accepts.

Derived on read from the membership's dates and its cancellation, with no stored column behind it.

Every value a membership program's `status` field can carry, and every value its `status` filter accepts.

Derived on read, with no stored column behind it.

Every value a payment's `status` field can carry, and every value its `status` filter accepts.

Derived from the internal deleted and voided flags, which are not exposed, so every payment maps onto exactly one of these three values.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 problem details describing an error response.

name.description: Gets the name. This is the column's name and the field name on the wire.

isDeleted.description:
Gets a value indicating whether the brand has been removed by the practice. Deleted brands stay in
this lookup because historical items still reference them; a consumer that only wants the currently
selectable brands filters on this field.

PublicBrand.description:
A brand: the practice-configurable list the inline `brand` reference on an item points at.
Property order is the wire order, and it is the field set PLA-1067 published — nothing more.

id.description: Gets the brand id. Tenant-local, and resolvable through `/v1/financials/item-brands`.

name.description: Gets the brand's name. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL`, and practice-renamable.

PublicBrandReference.description:
A brand, as it appears inline on an item. Two fields only; `/v1/financials/item-brands` carries the
    `isDeleted` flag.
    NEVER NULL. Items.BrandID is INT NOT NULL with a foreign key, so every item has one — and
THE NOT-SET SENTINEL HERE IS A NAME RATHER THAN AN ID. Brands is seeded (1,'Unknown') and
(2,'None'), so an item whose brand is unrecorded still points at a real row with a real id. Do not
read an id of 0 as "unset" — that convention belongs to the invoice and estimate aggregates, not
here — and do not translate 'Unknown' into null: the two seeded names mean different things
("nobody said" versus "deliberately none") and collapsing either loses that.

id.description: Gets the category id. This is the value one of an item's `categories[].id` refers to.

name.description:
Gets the name. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL` per the DACPAC, so this is `required` rather than
nullable.

PublicCategory.description:
A category: the practice-configurable list an item's `categories[]` entries point at.
    Property order is the wire order, and it is the whole table — Categories has exactly two columns,
CategoryID and Name, and both are published.
    This is the flat category list, not the hierarchical one: HierarchicalCategories is a separate
table with its own parentId and its own delete flag, served by its own lookup.

id.description: Gets the category id. Tenant-local, and resolvable through `/v1/financials/item-categories`.

name.description:
Gets the category's name. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL`, and practice-renamable.
    Categories HAS NO DELETE FLAG, so deletion there is hard AND CASCADES:
FK_ItemCategories_Categories is ON DELETE CASCADE, so deleting a category silently
removes it from every item that carried it. See GET /v1/financials/items for what that means for a change
feed.

PublicCategoryReference.description:
A category, as it appears in an item's `categories[]`. Two fields only; `/v1/financials/item-categories`
    carries the full set.
    Categories are a MANY-TO-MANY through ItemCategories, so an item can have none, one or many, and
the array is empty rather than null when it has none.

creditNoteNumber.description:
Gets the practice-facing credit note number. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL` with a uniqueness
constraint, so it is `required` rather than nullable.

patientId.description:
Gets the patient this credit note belongs to, or NULL when it belongs to no patient.
    A credit note CAN EXIST WITHOUT A PATIENT: CreditNotes.PatientID is INT NULL, which
makes this aggregate unique among the three — Invoices.PatientID and
Estimates.PatientID are both NOT NULL. A null here is the practice's data, not a bug
and not a redaction. It also means the patientId filter can never return such a credit note.

invoiceId.description:
Gets the invoice this credit note was raised against, or null when it was raised standalone.
`INT NULL` with `FK_CreditNotes_Invoices`, so the reference resolves through
`GET /v1/financials/invoices/{id}`.

patientCreditId.description:
Gets the patient credit this note is settled through, or null.
    A REFERENCE ONLY. The patient-credit aggregate is not part of the public surface in v1, so this id is
not resolvable yet; it is published because it is the join key a consumer will eventually need, and
because it distinguishes a credit note backed by a live patient credit from one that is not — which
is exactly the distinction decimal? PublicCreditNote.AppliedAsPaymentAmount and decimal? PublicCreditNote.RefundedAmount
being null carries.

serviceLocationId.description:
Gets the location the service was delivered at, or NULL when the practice never set one.
`ServiceLocationID` is `INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` in the database and 0 is a "not set"
sentinel rather than a location id, so it is published as `null`: returning 0 would name a
location that does not exist.

billingLocationId.description:
Gets the location the credit note is billed from, or NULL when the practice never set one. Same
`NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` sentinel as int? PublicCreditNote.ServiceLocationId.

effectiveDate.description: Gets the effective date. A `DATE` column — a calendar date with no time part.

createdUtcDate.description:
Gets the creation timestamp, in UTC.
    MAY BE 1900-01-01T00:00:00Z. The column is DATETIME NOT NULL with a
DEFAULT '1900-01-01', so a credit note written before the platform started recording creation
timestamps carries that sentinel rather than a real date. Such a row is returned like any other; if
it has also never been edited, DateTimeOffset PublicCreditNote.ModifiedDateUtc equals the sentinel and the row sits
permanently at the front of the change feed.

status.description:
Gets the lifecycle state. `Void` and `Deleted` credit notes ARE part of the feed and are
returned with their status, so filter on `status` rather than assuming a live-only collection.

subTotalAmount.description:
Gets the sub-total amount. GROSS of discount: the platform computes it as the line sub-totals with
decimal PublicCreditNote.TotalDiscount added back, so `subTotalAmount - totalDiscount` is the net figure
and this one is not.

totalDiscount.description: Gets the total discount applied across the credit note's lines.

amount.description:
Gets the credited total — what the practice gave back. Computed by the platform as
`subTotalAmount - totalDiscount + the credit note's tax total`, and that last term is the sum of
the unpublished `CreditNoteTaxes` rows, so on a taxed credit note this figure does NOT reconcile
from the published fields alone. It is authoritative; do not recompute it.

appliedAsPaymentAmount.description:
Gets how much of the credit has been spent as payment, or NULL.
    NUMERIC(18,2) NULL and published as nullable deliberately. The write path sets it to null —
not zero — when the credit note has no live patient credit behind it, so "never applied" and
"applied zero" are genuinely different facts and coalescing would assert the second when the first is
true. A consumer that wants a number must choose its own default and know it is choosing.
    Together with decimal? PublicCreditNote.RefundedAmount and decimal PublicCreditNote.Balance it accounts for
decimal PublicCreditNote.Amount: appliedAsPaymentAmount + refundedAmount + balance == amount, treating
each null as zero. That is a REAL invariant here, not a tautology — all four values are stored
independently in their own columns, unlike the invoice surface's paidAmount, which is derived
from amount - balanceDue and therefore closes by construction.

refundedAmount.description:
Gets how much of the credit was refunded in cash, or NULL, on exactly the same terms as
decimal? PublicCreditNote.AppliedAsPaymentAmount — the two are set and cleared together.

balance.description:
Gets the unconsumed remainder of the credit, as the platform maintains it against the linked patient
credit's outstanding amount. `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, so unlike the two figures above this one is
always a number: a credit note with no live patient credit reads `0` here and `null` there.

currency.description:
Gets the currency. Fixed `"USD"`: the platform stores no currency per credit note, so this
states the assumption every amount above is denominated in rather than leaving a consumer to infer it.

modifiedDateUtc.description:
Gets the change-feed watermark: `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)`, in UTC.
    NON-NULLABLE by construction. The stored ModifiedUtcDate is nullable and is null for every
credit note nobody has edited; publishing that directly would make those rows invisible to a consumer
syncing on it, so this field carries the coalesced value and equals createdUtcDate until the
first edit. The query parameter that filters on it is updatedSince — the asymmetry between the
two names is deliberate and platform-wide.

lineItems.description:
Gets the lines, ordered by `orderIndex` then id. Fetched set-based for the whole page: one query
for the headers and one for every line on the page.

PublicCreditNote.description:
A credit note: the header plus its lines.
    Property order is the wire order. The header drops CreatedByUserID, ModifiedByUserID, the
legacy nullable LocationID superseded by the service/billing pair, SharedWithPatient,
Reference, and the operator free text Notes, Reason and Description.
    CreditNoteTaxes, CreditNoteMemberships, CareCreditRequests and the
PatientCredit aggregate are never joined. The patient credit in particular: the internal read
attaches it with its whole AppliedPatientCredits collection, each carrying a nested
Payment, so int? PublicCreditNote.PatientCreditId is a REFERENCE ONLY and the applied and refunded
figures below come from the credit note's own columns rather than from that graph.
    THERE IS NO TAX FIELD ON THIS PAYLOAD, and a consumer must not read the absence as an implicit zero.
CreditNotes carries no tax column whatsoever: no TaxTotal, no
TaxableSubTotalAmount, no NonTaxableSubTotalAmount, and — unlike both Invoices and
Estimates — not even CoveredTaxesAmount. There is no SurchargesTotal and no
TipsTotal here either. A taxed credit note's tax sits in the CreditNoteTaxes breakdown
rows, which v1 drops, so it is unavailable rather than zero.
    There are no responsibleParties: no such table exists for credit notes at all, which is a
stronger statement than the one the invoice and estimate surfaces make, where the table exists and the
slice cuts it.

parentCreditNoteItemId.description:
Gets the line this one hangs under, or null when it is a top-level line. Package and adjustment lines
form a hierarchy. `FK_CreditNoteItems_ParentCreditNoteItems` keeps the reference resolvable
within `CreditNoteItems`, but it does NOT constrain the parent to the same credit note — so
resolve a parent within the `lineItems` array you were given rather than assuming it is there.

itemId.description: Gets the catalog item id this line was created from. Resolves through `GET /v1/financials/items/{id}`.

overrideName.description:
Gets the display name the practice typed on this line, or null when they typed none.
    OPERATOR-AUTHORED FREE TEXT and it MAY CONTAIN PHI, because a practice can type anything into it — a
procedure, a body site, or a patient's own words. Treat it as protected health information:
do not log it, do not put it in a cache key, do not index it for search, and do not display it
outside an authorized clinical or billing context.
    NVARCHAR(100) NULL per the DACPAC — nullable HERE, unlike the invoice and estimate lines where
the same column is NOT NULL. So null and an empty string are both reachable, and they
mean the same thing.

orderIndex.description:
Gets the position of this line within its credit note, ascending. `INT NOT NULL`, so always
present.

rate.description:
Gets the rate. A UNIT PRICE unless bool PublicCreditNoteLineItem.IsCalculatedRate is `true`, in which case this
IS the line total and multiplying by decimal PublicCreditNoteLineItem.Quantity is wrong.

isCalculatedRate.description:
Gets a value indicating whether decimal PublicCreditNoteLineItem.Rate is the line total rather than a unit price — the
    case a price schedule produces.
    When false: subTotalAmount = rate × quantity − totalDiscount. When true:
subTotalAmount derives from rate alone and the multiplication does not reconcile.
subTotalAmount is authoritative either way; this flag says which arithmetic applies, so a
consumer does not read a price-schedule line as an arithmetic bug. The column carries the identical
DDL comment to its invoice and estimate twins.

discountRate.description:
Gets the discount rate — a percentage when bool PublicCreditNoteLineItem.IsPercentDiscount is `true`, otherwise
an amount.

isPercentDiscount.description: Gets a value indicating whether decimal PublicCreditNoteLineItem.DiscountRate is a percentage.

totalDiscount.description: Gets the discount amount actually applied to this line.

oneOf.description:
Gets the discount reason, or null when the practice recorded none. The same inline `{id, name}`
object `/v1/financials/discount-reasons` returns: deletion on that table is HARD, so this inline copy
of the label is the only surviving record of a reason that has since been removed.

subTotalAmount.description:
Gets the sub-total amount, before taxes. AUTHORITATIVE — see bool PublicCreditNoteLineItem.IsCalculatedRate before
recomputing it.

amountPaid.description:
Gets how much of THIS LINE has been settled. `NUMERIC(18,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, so always a
number — unlike the header's `appliedAsPaymentAmount` and `refundedAmount`, which are
nullable. It exists only on credit note lines, and it is what makes per-line refund reconciliation
possible.

isExcludedFromTotal.description: Gets a value indicating whether this line is excluded from the credit note's totals.

providerId.description: Gets the provider attached to this line, or null.

providerSelectionType.description: Gets how the provider was attached.

salesPersonId.description: Gets the sales person attached to this line, or null.

PublicCreditNoteLineItem.description:
One line of a credit note.
    A DISTINCT type rather than one schema shared with the invoice or estimate line item, on the same reasoning
PLA-1061 and PLA-1060 settled: the middle of the three rows is nearly identical, but the EDGES are what a
shared component would have to lie about. AmountPaid and IsReturnable exist only on
CreditNoteItems; TotalTax exists on the other two and not here; BatchID is absent from
EstimateItems; OverrideName is nullable here and NOT NULL there; and neither
cross-reference column — EstimateItems.InvoiceID, InvoiceItems.EstimateItemID — has any
counterpart on this table. One shared component would need most of that optional and generic names for the
key and parent key that stop saying which entity they point at.
    Property order is the wire order. Description, TaxID, BatchID and
IsReturnable are not published. IsReturnable deserves the note: it is inventory-tracking
behaviour — the DDL says it decides "whether item can be returned into inventory (via inv. adjustment)" —
and inventory is out of v1, so publishing it would expose a behaviour flag whose surrounding contract does
not exist yet.

id.description: Gets the discount reason id. This is the value a line item's `discountReasonId` refers to.

name.description:
Gets the name. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL` per the DACPAC, so this is `required` rather than
nullable.

PublicDiscountReason.description:
A discount reason: the practice-configurable list a discount's `discountReasonId` points at.
    Property order is the wire order, and it is the whole table — DiscountReasons has exactly two
columns, DiscountReasonID and Name, and both are published.

estimateNumber.description:
Gets the practice-facing estimate number. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL` and unique per tenant, so it
is `required` rather than nullable.

patientId.description: Gets the patient this estimate belongs to.

appointmentId.description: Gets the appointment this estimate was raised from, or null.

serviceLocationId.description:
Gets the location the service is delivered at, or NULL when the practice never set one.
`ServiceLocationID` is `INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` in the database and 0 is a "not set"
sentinel rather than a location id, so it is published as `null`: returning 0 would name a
location that does not exist.

billingLocationId.description:
Gets the location the estimate is billed from, or NULL when the practice never set one. Same
`NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` sentinel as int? PublicEstimate.ServiceLocationId.

effectiveDate.description: Gets the effective date. A `DATE` column — a calendar date with no time part.

expiryDate.description: Gets the expiry date, or null when the estimate does not expire.

createdUtcDate.description: Gets the creation timestamp, in UTC.

status.description:
Gets the lifecycle state. Rejected, Cancelled and Deleted estimates ARE part of the feed — reporting
computes conversion rates from the whole population — so filter on `status` rather than assuming
a live-only collection.

estimateType.description: Gets whether this is a single estimate or a package.

subTotalAmount.description: Gets the sub-total amount, before taxes.

totalDiscount.description: Gets the total discount applied across the estimate.

coveredTaxesAmount.description:
Gets the tax amount the practice absorbs. The ONLY tax figure this contract publishes: there is no
`taxTotal`, no per-line `totalTax` — the column exists and the DDL says it is "not being
used for now" — and no join to `EstimateTaxes`, whose breakdown v1 drops.

patientCreditsAmount.description: Gets the patient credits applied to this estimate.

amount.description: Gets the total amount, including collected and not-collected lines.

currency.description:
Gets the currency. Fixed `"USD"`: the platform stores no currency per estimate, so this states
the assumption every amount above is denominated in rather than leaving a consumer to infer it.

invoiceIds.description:
Gets the distinct invoices any of this estimate's lines has been converted into, ascending; empty
    while nothing has been invoiced.
    Derived from the lines below, because conversion is PER LINE: EstimateItems.InvoiceID is
nullable and there is no InvoiceID on the estimate header at all. More than one id here, or one
id alongside a line whose invoiceId is null, means the estimate is PARTIALLY converted. Each id
is retrievable from /v1/financials/invoices/{id}.

modifiedDateUtc.description:
Gets the change-feed watermark: `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)`, in UTC.
    NON-NULLABLE by construction. The stored ModifiedUtcDate is nullable and is null for every
estimate nobody has edited; publishing that directly would make those rows invisible to a consumer
syncing on it, so this field carries the coalesced value and equals createdUtcDate until the
first edit. The query parameter that filters on it is updatedSince — the asymmetry between the
two names is deliberate and platform-wide.

lineItems.description:
Gets the lines, ordered by `orderIndex` then id. Fetched set-based for the whole page: one query
for the headers and one for every line on the page.

PublicEstimate.description:
An estimate: the header plus its lines.
    Property order is the wire order. The header drops OwnerID, CreatedByUserID,
ModifiedByUserID, the legacy LocationID superseded by the service/billing pair,
ProcedureAppointmentID, SubTotalAmountExcludingNotCollected,
UnDeliveredSubTotalAmount, TotalDuePractice, IsEditState,
DirtyEditByUserID/DirtyEditUtcDate, IncludeInsuranceOptions,
SharedWithPatient, UseCustomDescription, and the operator free text Notes,
LegalText, CustomDescription, Reason and Description.
    EstimateTaxes, EstimateMemberships, EstimateItemPatientCredits,
EstimateItemResponsibleParties and PatientSignatures are never joined. The signature table
in particular carries signature images and signer identity and does not appear on this surface in any
form.
    There is no revision or version column on Estimates, so the ticket's open question about
superseded estimate versions resolves itself: the schema keeps no history to expose or hide. An edit
overwrites the row and moves ModifiedUtcDate, which is exactly what the change feed reports.

parentEstimateItemId.description:
Gets the line this one hangs under, or null when it is a top-level line. Package lines form a
hierarchy; `FK_EstimateItems_ParentEstimateItems` keeps the reference resolvable, but only
within the same estimate's line set.

itemId.description: Gets the catalog item id this line was created from.

overrideName.description:
Gets the display name the practice typed on this line.
    OPERATOR-AUTHORED FREE TEXT and it MAY CONTAIN PHI, because a practice can type anything into it — a
procedure, a body site, or a patient's own words. Treat it as protected health information:
do not log it, do not put it in a cache key, do not index it for search, and do not display it
outside an authorized clinical or billing context.
    NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL per the DACPAC, so it is always present, though it may be an empty
string.

orderIndex.description: Gets the position of this line within its estimate, ascending.

rate.description:
Gets the rate. A UNIT PRICE unless bool PublicEstimateLineItem.IsCalculatedRate is `true`, in which case this
IS the line total and multiplying by decimal PublicEstimateLineItem.Quantity is wrong.

isCalculatedRate.description:
Gets a value indicating whether decimal PublicEstimateLineItem.Rate is the line total rather than a unit price — the
    case a price schedule produces.
    When false: subTotalAmount = rate × quantity − totalDiscount. When true:
subTotalAmount derives from rate alone and the multiplication does not reconcile.
subTotalAmount is authoritative either way; this flag says which arithmetic applies, so a
consumer does not read a price-schedule line as an arithmetic bug.

discountRate.description:
Gets the discount rate — a percentage when bool PublicEstimateLineItem.IsPercentDiscount is `true`, otherwise
an amount.

isPercentDiscount.description: Gets a value indicating whether decimal PublicEstimateLineItem.DiscountRate is a percentage.

totalDiscount.description: Gets the discount amount actually applied to this line.

oneOf.description:
Gets the discount reason, or null when the practice recorded none. The same inline `{id, name}`
object `/v1/financials/discount-reasons` returns: deletion on that table is HARD, so this inline copy
of the label is the only surviving record of a reason that has since been removed.

subTotalAmount.description:
Gets the sub-total amount, before taxes. AUTHORITATIVE — see bool PublicEstimateLineItem.IsCalculatedRate before
recomputing it.

isNotCollected.description: Gets a value indicating whether the practice flagged this line as not collected.

isExcludedFromTotal.description: Gets a value indicating whether this line is excluded from the estimate's totals.

providerId.description: Gets the provider attached to this line, or null.

providerSelectionType.description: Gets how the provider was attached.

salesPersonId.description: Gets the sales person attached to this line, or null.

invoiceId.description:
Gets the invoice this line was converted into, or null while it is still uninvoiced. This is the only
estimate-to-invoice linkage the schema carries — there is no `InvoiceID` on the estimate header —
which is why a package can be partially converted.

PublicEstimateLineItem.description:
One line of an estimate.
    A DISTINCT type rather than one schema shared with the invoice line item. PLA-1061 left the choice to
whichever slice landed first and this is it, decided by diffing the two tables.
    The middle of the two rows is genuinely identical — OverrideName, OrderIndex, provider and
sales person, Rate, IsCalculatedRate, Quantity, the discount trio,
DiscountReasonID, SubTotalAmount, Amount, IsExcludedFromTotal and
ProviderSelectionType all match, IsCalculatedRate down to the same DDL comment. The EDGES
are what differ, and they are the fields a shared component would have to lie about:
IsNotCollected exists only on EstimateItems; BatchID only on InvoiceItems;
and the cross-reference points in OPPOSITE directions — an estimate line names the invoice it became
(InvoiceID), while an invoice line names the estimate line it came from
(EstimateItems.EstimateItemID). Both tables do carry a self-referencing parent
(ParentEstimateItemID / ParentInvoiceItemID), but under different names, as do the primary
keys.
    One shared component therefore needs six fields optional, three of them always null on each side, and
generic names for the key and parent key that stop saying which entity they point at. Unpicking it later
is a breaking change for every generated client, so the two stay separate.
    Property order is the wire order. Description, TaxID, TotalTax,
QuantityDelivered, UnDeliveredSubTotalAmount and UseResponsibleParties are not
published, and neither are the EstimateItemResponsibleParties or
EstimateItemPatientCredits collections — the read path does not load any of them, so this record
cannot grow one by accident.

cardNumber.description:
Gets the card number, masked — never the stored value, because a gift card number is a redeemable
    instrument.
    The mask is length-aware, and hidden characters become * one for one so the original length is
preserved: 9 characters or more keeps the first 4 and last 4 (GC12****9012), 5 to 8 keeps the
last 4 (****5678), and 4 or fewer keeps nothing (****). It can be an empty string.

value.description:
Gets the remaining balance — what is still left to spend, not the face value, which is
    decimal? PublicGiftCard.MaxValue.
    Derived from the card's payment ledger, so it can go up as well as down: a refunded or reversed
redemption raises it. A card issued for 100 and never funded reads value: 0, and so does a fully
spent one — PublicGiftCardStatus PublicGiftCard.Status is what tells them apart.

maxValue.description:
Gets the face value the card was issued for, or null for a card with no stated maximum.
    The null is a real state: an open-value card has no ceiling. Do not read it as zero — "worth nothing"
and "no stated maximum" are opposites. Stored and stable for the life of the card; compare it with
decimal PublicGiftCard.Value for how much has been spent.

currency.description:
Gets the currency decimal PublicGiftCard.Value and decimal? PublicGiftCard.MaxValue are denominated in. Always
`"USD"` — the platform stores no per-card currency, so this is a stated assumption made explicit.

issuedDate.description:
Gets the date the card was issued. A calendar date with no time and no timezone, which is why the name
carries no `Utc` suffix. Never null, and the date the collection's range filter works on.

availabilityDate.description:
Gets the date the card becomes spendable, or null when it is spendable immediately. A calendar date.
    A real constraint rather than a label — the card cannot be spent before it. It plays no part in
PublicGiftCardStatus PublicGiftCard.Status, so a not-yet-available card reads Active; compare this date yourself if
you mean spendable today.

expirationDate.description:
Gets the date the card expires, or null for one that never does. A calendar date.
    The null is a real and common state: such a card is never Expired however old it is. When it is
set, the comparison is inclusive — a card whose expiration date is today has already expired.

occasion.description:
Gets the occasion the card was issued for. Never null. Two fields only;
`/v1/financials/gift-card-occasions` carries the rest.

purchaserPatientId.description: Gets the patient who bought the card. Never null — a card always has a purchaser.

holderPatientId.description:
Gets the patient the card was made out to, or null. A null does not mean unknown: it means the card has
no separate holder, so the card belongs to its purchaser.

description.description:
Gets the description the practice typed on the card, or null.
    Operator free text, and it may contain patient information — a practice can type anything into it. Do
not log it, put it in a cache key, index it for search, or display it outside an authorized clinical or
billing context. It ships because a gift card is meaningless to a practice without the note explaining
it.

isRefundable.description:
Gets whether the card's remaining balance is refunded to the purchaser when the card is deleted. On a
`Deleted` card with `isRefundable: true`, expect the balance to have been returned.

status.description:
Gets the card's state, merging the stored and the computed status into one field.
    Draft and Deleted are stored and take precedence over whatever the dates and the balance
say. This table has no delete flag — deletion is the status, and deleted cards stay in the feed.
Redeemed means issued and fully spent; an unfunded card reads Active, not
Redeemed, because nothing was ever spent. Expired means issued, not spent out, and
DateOnly? PublicGiftCard.ExpirationDate today or earlier. Active is everything else.
    Redeemed beats Expired. Both computed values derive only from fields this payload
publishes, so a consumer can always recompute them.
    Unknown is returned only if a stored status outside the known values is ever written, so a
strict client absorbs such a row instead of failing to deserialize the page. The status filter
rejects it.

createdUtcDate.description:
Gets when the card was created, in UTC — a genuine instant, which is why this field keeps its
`Utc` suffix where the three calendar dates above drop theirs.

modifiedDateUtc.description:
Gets the change-feed watermark, in UTC. Never null, and equal to DateTimeOffset PublicGiftCard.CreatedUtcDate until the
    first change.
    It moves when the ledger moves, which is what makes decimal PublicGiftCard.Value and the Redeemed arm of
PublicGiftCardStatus PublicGiftCard.Status safe to sync on: funding, spending and reversing either are stamped onto the card
deliberately.

PublicGiftCard.description:
A gift card. Header only: the card's payment ledger is not exposed as a collection — it reaches this
payload as decimal PublicGiftCard.Value and the `Redeemed` arm of PublicGiftCardStatus PublicGiftCard.Status, and redemption itself
shows up on `/v1/financials/payments`.

PublicGiftCardStatus.description:
Gift-card state. One merged field: the stored status and the computed processing status are not both
exposed. Expired and Redeemed are derived on read.

name.description:
Gets the name. `NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL` per the DACPAC, so this is `required` rather than
nullable.

parentId.description:
Gets the parent category id, or `null` for a root category. `ParentID INT NULL` per the
    DACPAC — a root category genuinely has no parent, so this is nullable rather than defaulted to 0.
    This id can point at a category whose own bool PublicHierarchicalCategory.IsDeleted is true, or at one a
consumer's own picker logic has filtered out: the write side validates that a parent id exists at
all, but never that it is still live. See the endpoint description for detail.

isDeleted.description:
Gets a value indicating whether the category has been removed by the practice. Deleted categories
stay in this lookup because a live child can still carry this row's id as its `parentId`; a
consumer that only wants the currently selectable categories filters on this field.

PublicHierarchicalCategory.description:
A hierarchical category: the practice-configurable tree an item's `hierarchicalCategory` reference
    points at.
    Property order is the wire order, and it is the field set PLA-1069 published — nothing more. The
collection is FLAT: this contract carries int? PublicHierarchicalCategory.ParentId so a consumer can assemble the tree
itself, but no nesting happens server-side. See HierarchicalCategoryEndpoints for
why.

id.description: Gets the hierarchical category id, resolvable through `/v1/financials/item-hierarchical-categories`.

name.description: Gets the category's name. `NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL`, and practice-renamable.

parentId.description:
Gets this category's own parent id, or null when it sits at the root.
    NOT PROOF THE PARENT IS LIVE, and not proof it exists.
HierarchicalCategories.ParentID HAS NO FOREIGN KEY AT ALL, and the internal write path validates
a parent through a lookup that carries no IsDeleted predicate — so a live category can sit under
a soft-deleted one, and the platform does not stop it. Resolve the id against
/v1/financials/item-hierarchical-categories, which publishes isDeleted, rather than assuming the
graph is consistent.

PublicHierarchicalCategoryReference.description:
A hierarchical category, as it appears inline on an item. Three fields; `/v1/financials/item-hierarchical-categories`
    carries the whole tree and the `isDeleted` flag.
    NULLABLE ON THE ITEM: Items.HierarchicalCategoryId is INT NULL, and a null means the item has
not been filed in the tree — a normal state, not missing data.

invoiceNumber.description:
Gets the practice-facing invoice number. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL` with a uniqueness constraint,
so it is `required` rather than nullable.

patientId.description: Gets the patient this invoice belongs to.

estimateId.description:
Gets the estimate this invoice was raised from, or null when it was raised directly.
    The header-level link exists in THIS direction only: Invoices.EstimateID is a real column with
a foreign key, while Estimates carries no InvoiceID. An estimate's conversion is
tracked per line instead, so an estimate can be partially invoiced and more than one invoice can name
the same estimate.

appointmentId.description: Gets the appointment this invoice was raised from, or null.

serviceLocationId.description:
Gets the location the service was delivered at, or NULL when the practice never set one.
`ServiceLocationID` is `INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` in the database and 0 is a "not set"
sentinel rather than a location id, so it is published as `null`: returning 0 would name a
location that does not exist.

billingLocationId.description:
Gets the location the invoice is billed from, or NULL when the practice never set one. Same
`NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` sentinel as int? PublicInvoice.ServiceLocationId.

effectiveDate.description: Gets the effective date. A `DATE` column — a calendar date with no time part.

dueDate.description:
Gets the due date. `DATE NOT NULL`, so unlike an estimate's expiry it is always present — every
invoice has a due date even when it equals the effective date.

createdUtcDate.description: Gets the creation timestamp, in UTC.

status.description:
Gets the lifecycle state. `Void` and `Deleted` invoices ARE part of the feed and are
returned with their status — reporting consumers need to see reversals — so filter on `status`
rather than assuming a live-only collection.

subTotalAmount.description:
Gets the sub-total amount. GROSS of discount: the platform computes it as the line sub-totals with
decimal PublicInvoice.TotalDiscount added back, so `subTotalAmount - totalDiscount` is the net figure
and this one is not.

totalDiscount.description: Gets the total discount applied across the invoice's lines.

coveredTaxesAmount.description:
Gets the tax amount the practice absorbs. The ONLY tax figure this contract publishes: there is no
`taxTotal` — no column holds one; the invoice's tax total is the sum of the `InvoiceTaxes`
rows, whose breakdown v1 drops — and no per-line `totalTax`, whose column carries the DDL
comment "not being used for now".
This is NOT the invoice's tax total and must not be substituted for one.

tipsTotal.description:
Gets the tips collected against this invoice. Accumulated from payment tips and NOT an addend of
decimal PublicInvoice.Amount — it is reported alongside the total, not inside it.

surchargesTotal.description:
Gets the card surcharges on this invoice. A restatement of a surcharge LINE that is already inside
IReadOnlyList<PublicInvoiceLineItem> PublicInvoice.LineItems, so adding it to decimal PublicInvoice.Amount would double-count it.

amount.description:
Gets the grand total. Computed by the platform as
`subTotalAmount - totalDiscount + the invoice's tax total`, and that last term is the sum of the
unpublished `InvoiceTaxes` rows — so on a taxed invoice this figure does NOT reconcile from the
published fields alone. It is authoritative; do not recompute it.

paidAmount.description:
Gets the amount settled so far, DERIVED as `amount - balanceDue`.
    Derived from the invoice's own maintained balance, NOT summed from the payment ledger. It is
therefore NOT a reconciliation against AllocatedPayments: summing the allocations would add a
per-page aggregate and could disagree with the decimal PublicInvoice.BalanceDue the platform maintains. A
consumer that needs payment-level detail must read the payments resource, which carries invoice ids
without per-invoice amounts — the payment × invoice split is intentionally not public.

balanceDue.description: Gets the outstanding balance, as the platform maintains it against the payment allocations.

currency.description:
Gets the currency. Fixed `"USD"`: the platform stores no currency per invoice, so this states
the assumption every amount above is denominated in rather than leaving a consumer to infer it.

modifiedDateUtc.description:
Gets the change-feed watermark: `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)`, in UTC.
    NON-NULLABLE by construction. The stored ModifiedUtcDate is nullable and is null for every
invoice nobody has edited; publishing that directly would make those rows invisible to a consumer
syncing on it, so this field carries the coalesced value and equals createdUtcDate until the
first edit. The query parameter that filters on it is updatedSince — the asymmetry between the
two names is deliberate and platform-wide.
    A LINE-ITEM edit moves this too. It did not before PLA-1060: the line-item write paths wrote
InvoiceItems and left the header alone, so a changed rate, quantity, discount or provider was
invisible to an incremental consumer. Those paths now stamp the parent.

lineItems.description:
Gets the lines, ordered by `orderIndex` then id. Fetched set-based for the whole page: one query
for the headers and one for every line on the page.

PublicInvoice.description:
An invoice: the header plus its lines.
    Property order is the wire order. The header drops CreatedByUserID, ModifiedByUserID, the
legacy nullable LocationID superseded by the service/billing pair, IsEditState,
DirtyEditByUserID/DirtyEditUtcDate, IncludeInsuranceOptions,
IsInsuranceRelated, IsPostedToGalderma, IsViewedByPatient,
SharedWithPatient, UseCustomDescription, and the operator free text Notes,
LegalText, CustomDescription, Reason, EditReason and Description.
    InvoiceTaxes, InvoiceMemberships, InvoiceCertificates,
InvoicePostedItems, InvoiceItemResponsibleParties,
PaymentInvoices/PaymentInvoiceItems, RecurringPayments, PaymentRequests and
CareCreditRequestInvoices are never joined. The payment side in particular: the internal
paymentInvoices[] collection nests a whole Payment object per allocation, so the
payment × invoice split is deliberately not public and decimal PublicInvoice.PaidAmount is a total only.
    Insurance is out of v1, which is why InvoiceItemResponsibleParties — the payer split across
Patient plus three insurance tiers plus Adjustment — is absent. It also drags in operator
free text, an authorization code, an insurance company id and a designation id. The estimate surface cut
the same table for the same reasons, and splitting the decision between the two aggregates is the one
outcome to avoid.

parentInvoiceItemId.description:
Gets the line this one hangs under, or null when it is a top-level line. Package and adjustment lines
form a hierarchy; the foreign key keeps the reference resolvable, but only within the same invoice's
line set.

estimateItemId.description:
Gets the estimate line this one was converted from, or null when the invoice was raised directly.
This is the line-level half of the estimate-to-invoice linkage; the header's `estimateId` is the
other.

itemId.description: Gets the catalog item id this line was created from.

overrideName.description:
Gets the display name the practice typed on this line.
    OPERATOR-AUTHORED FREE TEXT and it MAY CONTAIN PHI, because a practice can type anything into it — a
procedure, a body site, or a patient's own words. Treat it as protected health information:
do not log it, do not put it in a cache key, do not index it for search, and do not display it
outside an authorized clinical or billing context.
    NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL per the DACPAC, so it is always present, though it may be an empty
string.

orderIndex.description: Gets the position of this line within its invoice, ascending.

rate.description:
Gets the rate. A UNIT PRICE unless bool PublicInvoiceLineItem.IsCalculatedRate is `true`, in which case this
IS the line total and multiplying by decimal PublicInvoiceLineItem.Quantity is wrong.

isCalculatedRate.description:
Gets a value indicating whether decimal PublicInvoiceLineItem.Rate is the line total rather than a unit price — the
    case a price schedule produces.
    When false: subTotalAmount = rate × quantity − totalDiscount. When true:
subTotalAmount derives from rate alone and the multiplication does not reconcile.
subTotalAmount is authoritative either way; this flag says which arithmetic applies, so a
consumer does not read a price-schedule line as an arithmetic bug. The column carries the identical
DDL comment to its estimate twin.

discountRate.description:
Gets the discount rate — a percentage when bool PublicInvoiceLineItem.IsPercentDiscount is `true`, otherwise
an amount.

isPercentDiscount.description: Gets a value indicating whether decimal PublicInvoiceLineItem.DiscountRate is a percentage.

totalDiscount.description: Gets the discount amount actually applied to this line.

oneOf.description:
Gets the discount reason, or null when the practice recorded none. The same inline `{id, name}`
object `/v1/financials/discount-reasons` returns: deletion on that table is HARD, so this inline copy
of the label is the only surviving record of a reason that has since been removed.

subTotalAmount.description:
Gets the sub-total amount, before taxes. AUTHORITATIVE — see bool PublicInvoiceLineItem.IsCalculatedRate before
recomputing it.

isExcludedFromTotal.description: Gets a value indicating whether this line is excluded from the invoice's totals.

providerId.description: Gets the provider attached to this line, or null.

providerSelectionType.description: Gets how the provider was attached.

salesPersonId.description: Gets the sales person attached to this line, or null.

PublicInvoiceLineItem.description:
One line of an invoice.
    A DISTINCT type rather than one schema shared with the estimate line item. PLA-1061 settled that choice
and this slice keeps it: the middle of the two rows is genuinely identical, but the EDGES are what a
shared component would have to lie about. IsNotCollected exists only on EstimateItems;
BatchID only on InvoiceItems; and the cross-reference points in OPPOSITE directions — an
estimate line names the invoice it became, while an invoice line names the estimate line it came from.
One shared component needs six fields optional, three of them always null on each side, and generic
names for the key and parent key that stop saying which entity they point at. Unpicking that later is a
breaking change for every generated client.
    Property order is the wire order. Description, TaxID, TotalTax, BatchID and
UseResponsibleParties are not published, and neither is the
InvoiceItemResponsibleParties collection — the payer split insurance would need — nor
PaymentInvoiceItems. The read path does not load any of them, so this record cannot grow one by
accident.

name.description:
Gets the item's name. `required` over `NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL`: every item has one and it can
never be null, so a nullable type here would make every generated client null-check it for nothing.

sku.description:
Gets the item's stock-keeping unit, or null. `NVARCHAR(50) NULL`, and the null is common — a
service usually has no SKU. NOT unique: nothing in the schema constrains it, and the internal search
treats a SKU match and a UPC match interchangeably, so two items can share one.

description.description:
Gets the item's description, or null. `NVARCHAR(MAX) NULL`.
    CATALOG PRODUCT COPY, NOT A PATIENT NOTE, and that distinction is why this field ships plainly where
giftCard.description needed four controls and a contract exception. This text describes the
service or product itself and lives on a row shared by every patient ever billed for the item, so it
has no patient link to leak. The two accepted free-text PHI exposures on this surface remain
overrideName and giftCard.description, and this is not a third.
    It is still operator-authored, so it can contain whatever a practice typed. Treat it as untrusted
input for display purposes; it is not treated as PHI.

itemType.description: Gets the item's type. NEVER NULL — `ItemTypeID` is `INT NOT NULL` with a foreign key.

brand.description:
Gets the item's brand. NEVER NULL, and its not-set value is a NAME rather than an id — see
PublicBrandReference.

categories.description:
Gets the categories the item is filed under. EMPTY rather than null when it has none.
    A MANY-TO-MANY through ItemCategories, fetched set-based for a whole page — one query for the
page's links, not one per item. Independent of PublicHierarchicalCategoryReference? PublicItem.HierarchicalCategory, which is a
different, single-parent taxonomy: an item can be in both, either or neither.
    CHANGES HERE DO MOVE DateTimeOffset PublicItem.ModifiedDateUtc. Re-assigning an item's categories is a change to
junction rows rather than to the item, and the junction has no watermark of its own, so this slice made
the write stamp the item — otherwise an incremental consumer would hold a stale list forever. One
exception is documented on GET /v1/financials/items: deleting a CATEGORY cascades the links away without
stamping anything.

oneOf.description:
Gets the item's place in the hierarchical taxonomy, or NULL when it has not been filed in the tree.
The null is a normal state rather than missing data.

status.description:
Gets the item's status, as a NAME. `required` over `ItemStatuses.Name NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL`.
    A FLAT STRING WITH NO ID AND NO REFERENCE OBJECT, which is the shape PLA-1053 settled for all three of
this payload's FK'd labels: the referenced table is not on the public surface, so an id here would be a
key with nothing to resolve it against. The platform seeds four values — NotSet,
Active, Inactive, Backordered — but ItemStatuses is an ordinary
IDENTITY table with no constraint on its contents, so a practice's own value can appear and this
is NOT a closed vocabulary. There is no status lookup endpoint and no status filter; do not
switch on this string.
    IT IS NOT THE SAME THING AS bool PublicItem.IsForSale AND NOT THE SAME THING AS bool PublicItem.IsDeleted.
The practice's Active/Inactive toggle writes bool PublicItem.IsForSale and never touches this column, so
an item can perfectly well read status: "Active" and isForSale: false — that is the
normal state of an item a practice has stopped selling. See GET /v1/financials/items.

unit.description:
Gets the unit the item is measured in, as a NAME — `Units`, `Hours`, `Vials` and so on.
`required` over `Units.Name NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL`, a flat string on the same terms as
string PublicItem.Status. The unit may since have been soft-deleted by the practice, which this payload
does not show.

gender.description:
Gets the patient gender the item is restricted to, as a NAME, or NULL for an item usable with any
    patient.
    THE NULL IS THE COMMON CASE and it means "no restriction", not "unknown". Items.GenderID is
INT NULL and the internal filter treats a null as "may be used for any patient".
    A NAME RATHER THAN AN INTEGER, deliberately: the platform's own DDL comment on that column and its own
seed script disagree about which integer means Other, so any consumer mapping the number would
be picking one of two contradictory sources. The name comes straight from Genders.Name, so this
contract never has to take a side. Not a closed vocabulary, for the same reason as
string PublicItem.Status.

serviceType.description:
Gets how the item is classified for service reporting. `TINYINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, and
`Undefined` is BOTH the stored default and the out-of-contract sentinel — most items carry it
because nothing forces a practice to classify one.

providerSelectionType.description:
Gets how a provider is attached to the item. `INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, and
`NotSelected` is both the stored default and the sentinel.
User is the only value for which int? PublicItem.PreferredProviderId is meaningful.

preferredProviderId.description:
Gets the practice user preferred as the item's provider, or null. `INT NULL` with NO foreign key —
the user lives in another service, so this id is not resolvable anywhere on this surface and the
platform does not guarantee the user still exists.

flatPrice.description:
Gets the item's GLOBAL LIST PRICE, or NULL when none is set.
    NOT THE PRICE ANYONE PAYS, and this is the most likely misreading of this payload. Three things
override it and none of them is published in v1: a per-location price
(LocationItemInventory.FlatPrice), a tiered schedule keyed on quantity and location
(PriceSchedules, used whenever the item's price type is per-tier), and any discount or override
applied on the document itself. THE PRICE ACTUALLY CHARGED LIVES ON THE INVOICE LINE — read
/v1/financials/invoices or /v1/financials/estimates for that.
    The NULL is a real state, not zero: an item priced only through tiers has no flat price at all, and
reading a null as 0 would say "free" where the data says "priced elsewhere".

currency.description:
Gets the currency decimal? PublicItem.FlatPrice is denominated in. Always `"USD"`: the platform stores
no per-item currency, so this is a stated assumption made explicit rather than a column, and it is the
same assumption every amount on this surface rests on.

isForSale.description:
Gets whether the item is currently offered for sale. `BIT NOT NULL`.
    THIS IS WHAT THE PRACTICE'S ACTIVE/INACTIVE TOGGLE WRITES. The internal toggle labelled "Active" and
"Inactive" sets this column and leaves string PublicItem.Status alone, so this — not string PublicItem.Status —
is the field to read for "is the practice selling this", and it is the only one of the three
availability flags this resource lets you filter on.
    INDEPENDENT OF bool PublicItem.IsDeleted. Deleting an item writes that flag and leaves this one as it
was, so a deleted item can read isForSale: true. Check both.

isNotCollected.description:
Gets whether payment for the item is not collected — a fee recorded on a document without being billed.
`BIT NOT NULL`.

isExcludedFromTotal.description:
Gets whether the item is left out of a document's total. `BIT NOT NULL`. Distinct from
bool PublicItem.IsNotCollected: this one affects the arithmetic, that one affects collection.

isDeleted.description:
Gets whether the item has been deleted by the practice. `BIT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` — a SOFT delete.
    DELETED ITEMS ARE RETURNED, carrying this flag. One that vanished from an incremental feed would leave
a consumer with a catalog entry it can never retire, and every invoice, estimate and credit-note line
ever written against the item still names it, so the row has to stay resolvable. There is no
server-side filter for it: read the flag.

parentItemId.description:
Gets the parent item's id for a bundled child item, or null. `INT NULL`, a self-reference within
    `Items`.
    An id only, never a nested item: the parent is a full item in its own right and is readable from this
same feed. Note that a change to the PARENT does not move this item's watermark, so treat the link as a
pointer to fetch rather than as a snapshot.

createdUtcDate.description:
Gets when the item was created, in UTC. `DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT GETUTCDATE()` and a genuine
instant, which is why this field keeps its `Utc` suffix.

modifiedDateUtc.description:
Gets the change-feed watermark: `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)`, in UTC.
    NON-NULLABLE by construction. The stored modified timestamp IS nullable and is null for every item
nobody has edited since it was created, so publishing that column directly would make a large
population invisible to a consumer syncing on it. This field carries the coalesced value and equals
DateTimeOffset PublicItem.CreatedUtcDate until the first change.
    The query parameter that filters on it is updatedSince; the asymmetry between the two names is
deliberate and platform-wide. Two changes do NOT move it, both documented on GET /v1/financials/items:
deleting a Category, and deleting a hierarchical category.

PublicItem.description:
A catalog item — a service or product a practice sells.
    THE ONLY RESOURCE ON THIS SURFACE THAT IS NOT PATIENT-LINKED except membership programmes: an item is a
practice's configuration, shared by every patient ever billed for it, and no field on this payload
identifies a patient. That is why description ships unconditionally where the gift-card
description needed four controls, and why the disclosure audit records carriedFreeText: false.
    Property order is the wire order. Dropped from the stored row, on top of the shared conventions:
trackInventoryMode, priceType and parentChildType (the enums behind them are out of
v1); purchaseInfo, so cost of goods and margin are not published at all; pictures[], which
is v2; cptCodeSettings, which is insurance coding; apxId, galdermaProductId and
baseItemId, which are third-party ids and internal catalog plumbing; salesAccountId, which
is ledger wiring; the per-location and tiered prices; all inventory; and
CreatedByUserID / ModifiedByUserID.

name.description:
Gets the group's name. `required` over `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL`. The only descriptive field on
the table: there is no description column and no code.

isActive.description:
Gets whether the group is active. `BIT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`.
    A REAL STORED COLUMN, unlike the item resource's requirement for the same filter — Items has no
such column and three orthogonal flags instead. Here the word means what it says.
    INDEPENDENT OF bool PublicItemGroup.IsDeleted: deleting a group does not clear this flag, so a deleted group
can read isActive: true. Check both.

isDeleted.description:
Gets whether the group has been deleted by the practice. `BIT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` — a SOFT delete,
so the row survives and is returned carrying this flag. There is no server-side filter for it.

details.description:
Gets the items the group contains, with the quantity of each. EMPTY rather than null for a group with
    no members, which is a real state — nothing requires a group to contain anything.
    INLINE, and fetched set-based for a whole page: one query for the page's details, not one per group.
Because they are inline, a change to any detail row moves DateTimeOffset PublicItemGroup.ModifiedDateUtc — see there.

createdUtcDate.description:
Gets when the group was created, in UTC. `DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT GETUTCDATE()`, a genuine
instant.

modifiedDateUtc.description:
Gets the change-feed watermark: `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)`, in UTC.
    IT MOVES WHEN A DETAIL MOVES, which is what makes the inline IReadOnlyList<PublicItemGroupDetail> PublicItemGroup.Details collection safe to
sync on incrementally. Adding, changing or removing a member item is a change to a child row rather
than to the group, so it is stamped onto the group's watermark deliberately, at the one repository seam
every write path shares — including the cascade that fires when the underlying catalog item is deleted.
    NON-NULLABLE by construction, and equal to DateTimeOffset PublicItemGroup.CreatedUtcDate until the first change. The
query parameter that filters on it is updatedSince.

PublicItemGroup.description:
An item group — a named bundle of catalog items a practice can add to a document in one action.
    THE SMALLEST PAYLOAD ON THIS SURFACE, and deliberately smaller than the requirement asked for. Four of
the fields in the requirement are not here — isForSale, subtotalAmount,
discountAmount and totalPrice, plus the currency that existed only to qualify the
last three — because none of them is a column on ItemGroups and none of them can be computed from
anything this contract publishes. GET /v1/financials/item-groups says so in prose rather than leaving a consumer
to notice the absence.
    Property order is the wire order.

itemId.description:
Gets the item this member names. `INT NOT NULL` with a foreign key to `Items`, so it always
resolves on `/v1/financials/items` — where its own `isDeleted` flag lives. A GROUP CAN NAME A DELETED
ITEM: deletion of an item is soft and cascades to nothing here, so check the item's flag rather than
assuming a group only contains live items.

quantity.description:
Gets how many of the item the group includes, or NULL when no quantity was ever set.
    NUMERIC(9,2) NULL, and the null is a real stored state: nothing on the write path requires a
quantity. It is published as null rather than coalesced to zero because "never set" and "zero" are
different facts and only the row knows which it holds — the internal calculator happens to read a null
as zero when it multiplies, but that is its arithmetic's convention rather than the data's meaning.

PublicItemGroupDetail.description:
One member of an item group: which item, and how many of it.
    TWO FIELDS, and the omissions are decisions rather than oversights. The detail row's own id is not
published because a detail is not addressable on this surface. Its price, discount and
type are not published because the group's money amounts are not, and those three exist only to
compute them — see GET /v1/financials/item-groups for why the amounts are withheld. Publishing the inputs to an
arithmetic whose output this contract cannot state would invite a consumer to reconstruct it from an
incomplete set of terms.

id.description: Gets the item type id. This is the value the inline `itemType.id` refers to.

name.description:
Gets the name. `VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL` per the DACPAC, so this is `required` rather than
nullable.

PublicItemType.description:
An item type: the practice-configurable classification an item's inline `itemType { id, name }`
    reference object points at.
    Property order is the wire order and matches the inline object exactly. The four behaviour flags on the
stored row — ShowInventory, ShowPaymentSchedules, ShowCollection, IsSelectable
— drive internal UI behaviour, not the meaning of the type, and are never published: PLA-1053 already
strips them from the inline object, and this endpoint agrees with that shape.
    Seeded defaults exist (DefaultItemTypes), but the set is tenant-extensible, so there is
deliberately no enum here.

id.description: Gets the item type id. Tenant-local, and resolvable through `/v1/financials/item-types`.

name.description:
Gets the item type's name. `VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL`, and practice-renamable — show it, group on the
    id.
    ItemTypes HAS NO DELETE FLAG of any kind, so deletion there is hard and this inline name is the
only surviving label for an item type a practice has removed.

PublicItemTypeReference.description:
An item type, as it appears inline on an item. Two fields only; `/v1/financials/item-types` carries the
    rest.
    NEVER NULL on an item: Items.ItemTypeID is INT NOT NULL with a foreign key, so it always
resolves.

membershipProgramId.description:
Gets the programme this membership is enrolled in.
    A REFERENCE, NOT PROOF THE PROGRAMME IS AVAILABLE. MembershipProgramID is INT NOT NULL
with FK_Memberships_MembershipPrograms, so it always names a row — but that programme may be
disabled, may have ended, and may since have been HARD-DELETED, in which case
/v1/financials/membership-programs/{id} answers 404 while this id keeps pointing at it. Resolve it there if
you need its state; nothing on this payload describes it.

patientId.description:
Gets the patient. `INT NOT NULL` — unlike a payment or a credit note, a membership always belongs
to someone, so this is never null and there is no not-set sentinel.

startDate.description:
Gets the date the membership starts.
    A CALENDAR DATE. The stored column is DATETIME NOT NULL rather than DATE, and the write
path truncates it to midnight on insert; the time part is not published and plays no part in
PublicMembershipStatus PublicMembership.Status.
    THIS MAY BE IN THE FUTURE while PublicMembershipStatus PublicMembership.Status reads Active — see the remarks on that
field. A consumer that means "in force today" has to check this date itself.

expirationDate.description:
Gets the date the membership expires, or NULL for one that never does.
    DATETIME NULL, published as a calendar date on the same terms as DateOnly PublicMembership.StartDate. The
null is a real and common state, not a missing value: it means no expiry was set, and such a
membership is never Expired.

assignedByUserId.description:
Gets the practice user who enrolled the patient. `AssignedBy INT NOT NULL`, with no foreign key —
the users live in another service, and this contract does not resolve the name.

assignedDateUtc.description:
Gets when the enrolment was recorded, in UTC. `AssignedDate DATETIME NOT NULL`, and unlike
DateOnly PublicMembership.StartDate it genuinely is an instant: the only write path sets it from
`DateTime.UtcNow`.

isPaid.description: Gets a value indicating whether the enrolment has been paid for. `BIT NOT NULL`.

isCancelled.description:
Gets a value indicating whether the membership was cancelled. `BIT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`.
    PUBLISHED AS ITSELF AND FOLDED INTO PublicMembershipStatus PublicMembership.Status, which is deliberately different from the
payment slice — where the two stored flags are hidden because they are INDEPENDENT and the precedence
between them would be a second thing to explain. Here there is only one flag and it is the top of the
precedence, so isCancelled == true and status == Cancelled are the same fact stated
twice, always and in both directions. It ships because the requirement asks for it.

invoiceId.description:
Gets the invoice the enrolment was billed on, or NULL. `INT NULL` with
`FK_Memberships_Invoice`. A REFERENCE ONLY, resolvable through `/v1/financials/invoices/{id}`.

giftCardId.description:
Gets the gift card granted with the enrolment, or NULL. `INT NULL` with
`FK_Memberships_GiftCard`. A REFERENCE ONLY — the gift card's NUMBER is neither published nor
read; resolve it through `/v1/financials/gift-cards/{id}`.

status.description:
Gets the lifecycle state. SYNTHESIZED — no column holds it.
    THREE of the enum's four values are produced, and they partition the collection in this precedence:
Cancelled, then Expired, then Active. Every one is computed from fields THIS
PAYLOAD PUBLISHES, which is the property that makes them safe in a change feed — a consumer can always
recompute them:
    * Cancelled — bool PublicMembership.IsCancelled is set, whatever the dates
    say.
* Expired — DateOnly? PublicMembership.ExpirationDate is set and is before today (UTC). A
    null expiration date never expires.
* Active — neither of the above.
    Past IS RESERVED AND NEVER RETURNED. It would mean "superseded by a later membership", which is
a fact about a DIFFERENT row — and enrolling a patient again does not modify the membership it
supersedes, so this row's ModifiedDateUtc would not move and an incremental consumer would keep
two Active memberships for one patient with nothing in the feed to reveal it. Group by
int PublicMembership.PatientId and int PublicMembership.MembershipProgramId and order by DateOnly PublicMembership.StartDate to
derive it yourself; all three are published. PLA-1077.
    Active INCLUDES A MEMBERSHIP THAT HAS NOT STARTED YET. DateOnly PublicMembership.StartDate plays no part in
the rule, because the published vocabulary has no "pending" value to give instead. Check
DateOnly PublicMembership.StartDate if you mean "in force today".
    It also IGNORES THE PROGRAMME'S TYPE, which the internal membership report does not: that report's
filter treats any membership in a PARTNER programme as active regardless of its dates or its
cancellation. Neither MembershipPrograms.Type nor PartnerId is published in v1, so
honouring that would return Active on a membership whose published dates say otherwise with
nothing here to explain it. The two therefore disagree for partner programmes, and this contract's
answer is the one derivable from what it publishes.
    Cancelled memberships ARE part of the feed and are returned with their status; filter on
status rather than assuming a live-only collection.

createdUtcDate.description:
Gets the creation timestamp, in UTC.
    DATETIME NOT NULL, added by PLA-1062 and BACKFILLED FROM AssignedDate — so for every
membership enrolled before that migration this equals DateTimeOffset PublicMembership.AssignedDateUtc EXACTLY, to the
tick. Do not read significance into the two agreeing on a historical row; they are the same number.

modifiedDateUtc.description:
Gets the change-feed watermark: `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)`, in UTC.
    NON-NULLABLE by construction. The stored ModifiedUtcDate is nullable and is null for every
membership nobody has cancelled, extended or paid for since PLA-1062 landed — which is nearly all of
them — so publishing that column directly would make the ordinary population invisible to a consumer
syncing on it. This field carries the coalesced value and equals DateTimeOffset PublicMembership.CreatedUtcDate until
the first edit. The query parameter that filters on it is updatedSince; the asymmetry between
the two names is deliberate and platform-wide.

PublicMembership.description:
A patient's enrolment in a membership programme. A HEADER ONLY — a membership has no child collection of
    any kind in the schema.
    Property order is the wire order. Nothing is dropped from the stored row except the three navigations
(MembershipProgram, GiftCard, Invoice), which ship as ids: this is the narrowest
table on the surface and there is no operator free text, no money and no denormalized name on it at all.
    THE PROGRAMME, THE GIFT CARD AND THE INVOICE ARE IDS, NEVER NESTED. In particular no gift card NUMBER is
published or even read — giftCardId is the reference and /v1/financials/gift-cards is where a consumer
resolves it.

membershipProgramId.description:
Gets the membership programme id. TENANT-LOCAL: it is an identity column in each practice's
    own database, so the same number means different programmes in two tenants.

name.description:
Gets the programme's name. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL`, so `required` rather than nullable.
    PRACTICE-AUTHORED AND RENAMABLE, but NOT per-record prose: one programme is created once and every
enrolment points at the same row, so this is a configuration label of the same kind as
paymentMode.name rather than text typed about a patient. Show it; do not group on it across
tenants, and do not treat it as an identifier.

price.description: Gets the enrolment price. `NUMERIC(18,2) NOT NULL`.

currency.description:
Gets the currency. Fixed `"USD"`: the platform stores no currency per programme, so this states
the assumption decimal PublicMembershipProgram.Price and decimal? PublicMembershipProgram.GiftCardAmount are denominated in rather than
leaving a consumer to infer it.

duration.description:
Gets the programme's configured duration. `INT NOT NULL`.
    THE UNIT IS NOT RECORDED ANYWHERE AND THIS SERVICE NEVER USES THE NUMBER. There is no expiration
arithmetic in the financials service at all: Memberships.ExpirationDate is a stored column set
by the enrolling caller, not computed from this. So this is descriptive metadata the practice
configured — treat it as a label to display, never as a term to compute an expiry from. A membership's
own expirationDate is the authoritative answer.

startDate.description:
Gets the date the programme becomes available for enrolment.
    A CALENDAR DATE. The stored column is DATETIME NOT NULL rather than DATE and nothing
truncates it on write, so a time part can exist; it is not published and plays no part in
PublicMembershipProgramStatus PublicMembershipProgram.Status, which is evaluated by calendar date.

endDate.description:
Gets the date the programme stops being available, or NULL for open-ended. `DATETIME NULL`,
published as a calendar date on the same terms as DateOnly PublicMembershipProgram.StartDate.

itemId.description:
Gets the catalog item the programme is sold as, or NULL.
    ItemID INT NULL with FK_MembershipPrograms_Items, so the null is a REAL STATE — a
programme configured without a catalog item — and not a redaction. A REFERENCE ONLY: the item is
never joined, so no item name or price reaches this payload.

giftCardAmount.description:
Gets the gift card amount granted on enrolment, or NULL.
    NUMERIC(18,2) NULL and published as nullable deliberately: "this programme grants no gift card"
and "it grants one worth zero" are different facts, and coalescing the first into the second asserts
something that is not true. A consumer that wants a number must choose its own default and know it is
choosing.

status.description:
Gets the availability state. SYNTHESIZED — no column holds it.
    Active means AVAILABLE FOR ENROLMENT: the practice has the programme switched on (the stored
IsEnabled flag, which is not published as itself) AND today falls inside the
DateOnly PublicMembershipProgram.StartDate … DateOnly? PublicMembershipProgram.EndDate window, both bounds inclusive by calendar date in UTC.
Inactive is the exact negation — switched off, not started yet, or already ended — so the two
values partition the collection and a consumer can recompute both from this payload.
    Disabled and ended programmes ARE part of the feed and are returned with their status; filter on
