status rather than assuming a live-only collection.

createdUtcDate.description:
Gets the creation timestamp, in UTC.
    DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT GETUTCDATE(), added by PLA-1062. FOR EVERY PROGRAMME THAT EXISTED
BEFORE THAT MIGRATION THIS IS THE TIMESTAMP THE COLUMN WAS ADDED, not a real creation date — there was
nothing to backfill it from, unlike a membership, which had AssignedDate. So a whole practice's
programmes commonly share one value that is unrelated to when they were configured. Use
DateOnly PublicMembershipProgram.StartDate for when the offering began.

modifiedDateUtc.description:
Gets the change-feed watermark: `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)`, in UTC.
    NON-NULLABLE by construction. The stored ModifiedUtcDate is nullable and is null for every
programme nobody has edited since PLA-1062 landed, so publishing that column directly would make the
whole population invisible to a consumer syncing on it. This field carries the coalesced value and
equals DateTimeOffset PublicMembershipProgram.CreatedUtcDate until the first edit. The query parameter that filters on it is
updatedSince; the asymmetry between the two names is deliberate and platform-wide.
    A DELETED PROGRAMME NEVER APPEARS HERE AT ALL, in any form. Deletion on this table is a HARD delete
and there is no IsDeleted column, so no row survives to carry a watermark and no change feed
can report the disappearance. See the endpoint description.

PublicMembershipProgram.description:
A membership programme — the practice-configured offering a patient enrols in. A HEADER ONLY.
    Property order is the wire order. The header drops the whole discounts[] collection and the three
obsolete discount triples (ServiceDiscount*, ProductDiscount*, FeeDiscount*): the
enums that gave a discount its meaning — what it applies to, and whether the amount is a rate or a sum —
are all out of v1, and a discount without its target is not interpretable. It also drops
applicationType, isCombineEnabled and the obsolete type, the partner integration
(partnerId and the partner extended information), iconId because media is v2, and the
isEnabled flag, which folds into PublicMembershipProgramStatus PublicMembershipProgram.Status.
    NO NESTED ITEM. int? PublicMembershipProgram.ItemId is a reference; the catalog item is never joined, so no item name,
price or classification reaches this payload.

PublicMembershipProgramStatus.description: Membership-program state. Synthesized — no stored column carries it.

PublicMembershipStatus.description: Patient membership state. Synthesized — no stored column carries it.

name.description: Gets the name. This is the column's name and the field name on the wire.

isSystem.description:
Gets a value indicating whether this is one of the platform-seeded occasions rather than one the
practice created.

isActive.description:
Gets a value indicating whether the occasion is active. Inactive occasions stay in this lookup: the
table has no audit columns, so there is no other way for a consumer to notice a practice turned one
off.

isDeleted.description:
Gets a value indicating whether the occasion has been removed by the practice. Deleted occasions
stay in this lookup because historical records still reference them; a consumer that only wants the
currently selectable occasions filters on this field.

PublicOccasion.description:
An occasion: the practice-configurable list a gift card's occasion id points at.
    Property order is the wire order, and it is the field set PLA-1066 published — nothing more. There is
deliberately no closed enum here: the stored OccasionEnum only covers the four seeded rows, the
set is tenant-extensible, and a closed contract enum would be wrong the first time a practice adds one.
isSystem is how a consumer distinguishes a seeded occasion from a practice-created one.

id.description:
Gets the occasion id. TENANT-LOCAL for anything a practice created — `Occasions.Id` is
    `IDENTITY(100, 1)` in each practice's own database, so a value of 100 or above means different
    things in two tenants. The four values BELOW 100 are platform-seeded and do mean the same everywhere.
    0 IS ONE OF THOSE SEEDED VALUES, not a not-set sentinel: it is 'Other', inserted by the
DACPAC's post-deployment script and the id every card with an unrecognised occasion was repointed at.
It is deliberately NOT rewritten as null, which is what the invoice, estimate and credit-note surfaces
do with their location columns.

name.description:
Gets the occasion's name. `VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL`, so `required` rather than nullable.
PRACTICE-RENAMABLE for anything a practice created: it is what someone typed, it can change under a
consumer at any time, and two practices' names for the same idea rarely agree. Show it; do not group
on it. It may also name an occasion the practice has since turned off or deleted — historical cards
keep pointing at it, and `/v1/financials/gift-card-occasions` is where those flags live.

PublicOccasionReference.description:
The occasion a gift card was issued for, inline on the gift-card payload.
    A DISTINCT type from PublicOccasion, which /v1/financials/gift-card-occasions returns. That record
publishes five fields — it adds isSystem, isActive and isDeleted, which are about how
the practice MANAGES its list of occasions, not about this card. Reusing it here would put three fields on
every gift card that say nothing about that card, and would make the lookup's field set un-evolvable:
adding a field there would silently widen this payload. Same reasoning, and the same shape, as
PublicPaymentModeReference on the payment surface.
    NEVER NULL on a gift card. GiftCards.OccasionId is INT NOT NULL with
FK_GiftCards_Occasions_OccasionId, so it always names a row — which is why this is a required
property rather than a nullable object, and why the query can join rather than left-join.

patientId.description:
Gets the patient this payment belongs to, or NULL when it belongs to no patient.
    A PAYMENT CAN EXIST WITHOUT A PATIENT: Payments.PatientID is INT NULL, and the case that
produces it is an INSURANCE PAYMENT, which carries an insurance company instead. That id —
InsuranceCompanyID — is NOT published in v1, so when this field is null the contract does not
tell you whose payment it is. Stated plainly rather than left to be inferred: a null here is neither a
redaction nor a bug, and it cannot be resolved from anything else on this payload.
    The consequence for paging is concrete: the patientId FILTER can never return such a payment, so
a consumer syncing patient by patient will never see the insurance payments and must page the
unfiltered feed to reach them.

locationId.description:
Gets the location the payment was taken at. `INT NOT NULL` — so unlike the location fields on the
invoice, estimate and credit-note payloads this one is never null and never carries a `0`
not-set sentinel: those three columns are `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and this one has no default.

paymentDate.description:
Gets the transaction date — the date the practice recorded the payment against, which is what a daily
collections total is bucketed by. A `DATE` column: a calendar date with no time part and no
timezone. Distinct from DateTimeOffset PublicPayment.CreatedUtcDate, which is when the row was written.

createdUtcDate.description:
Gets the creation timestamp, in UTC. `DATETIME NOT NULL` with no default constraint on this
table, so — unlike a credit note — a payment never carries a `1900-01-01` sentinel here.

amount.description:
Gets the amount taken. `NUMERIC(18,2) NOT NULL`.
    THE DIRECTION IS IN bool PublicPayment.IsRefund, NOT IN THE SIGN. A refund is recorded as an amount with the
refund flag set rather than as a negative number, and the insurance write path normalises a negative
input to its absolute value before storing it. So a consumer netting collections must subtract the
refunds it identifies by the flag; summing this column and trusting the signs to cancel would
double-count them.
    It is the GROSS figure the practice took, INCLUSIVE of decimal? PublicPayment.SurchargeAmount and of any tip:
the payment's tips are not published, so amount minus the surcharge is not the invoice-applied
total either. The per-invoice split is not on this payload at all — see IReadOnlyList<int> PublicPayment.InvoiceIds.

surchargeAmount.description:
Gets the surcharge charged on top of the payment, or NULL.
    NUMERIC(18,2) NULL and published as nullable deliberately: "no surcharge was charged" and "a
surcharge of zero was charged" are different facts, and coalescing the first into the second asserts
something that is not true. A consumer that wants a number must choose its own default and know it is
choosing.

currency.description:
Gets the currency. Fixed `"USD"`: the platform stores no currency per payment, so this states the
assumption decimal PublicPayment.Amount and decimal? PublicPayment.SurchargeAmount are denominated in rather than
leaving a consumer to infer it.

isRefund.description:
Gets a value indicating whether this row is a refund rather than a collection. `BIT NOT NULL`. The
sign is NOT in decimal PublicPayment.Amount, which is positive either way, so this flag is the only thing that
says which direction the money moved.

status.description:
Gets the lifecycle state. SYNTHESIZED — no column holds it.
    The stored IsDeleted and IsVoided flags are independent BIT NOT NULL columns and
BOTH CAN BE TRUE. When they are, this reads Deleted: deletion is the more terminal fact, and a
consumer filtering deleted payments out must not meet the same payment again as a voided one. So the
three values are a partition, and Voided means voided AND NOT deleted.
    Deleted and voided payments ARE part of the feed and are returned with their status; filter on
status rather than assuming a live-only collection.

paymentMode.description:
Gets the payment method, inline. Never null: `PaymentModeID` is `INT NOT NULL` with
`FK_Payments_PaymentModes`, so every payment has one and it always resolves — including when the
practice has since removed the mode, because `/v1/financials/payment-modes` keeps deleted rows.

oneOf.description:
Gets the reason the payment was recorded under, or NULL when the practice recorded none.
`PaymentReasonID` is `INT NULL`, so the whole object is null — never an empty object and
never an object with a blank description.

Gets the card brand, or NULL when this payment has no credit-card row — which is every cash, check,
    patient-credit, gift-card and rewards payment.
    A SCALAR, not a nested object. The card's other stored attributes — cardholder name, card reference,
vault id, gateway and processor sub-type — are not published and are not even read.
    Unknown is a REAL RETURNED VALUE here, not an inbound-only sentinel like the one on the status
enums: it means the brand was not recorded, which is what the gateway integration writes when it gets
a brand string it does not recognise. So null means "not a card payment" and Unknown
means "a card payment whose brand nobody recorded" — different facts, kept apart.

providerId.description: Gets the provider credited with the payment, or null. `INT NULL`.

invoiceIds.description:
Gets the invoices this payment is applied to. REFERENCES ONLY, and possibly empty.
    NO PER-ALLOCATION AMOUNTS. PaymentInvoices.Amount exists and is deliberately not published: the
split of one payment across several invoices is not part of the public contract, and per-invoice
reconciliation is done from the invoice side, through invoice.paidAmount. So on a payment with
more than one id here, this payload says WHICH invoices were paid and decimal PublicPayment.Amount says how
much in total, and nothing says how the total divides.
    SOFT-DELETED ALLOCATIONS ARE EXCLUDED. PaymentInvoices carries its own delete flag and the
unallocate path sets it, so an invoice a payment was unlinked from does not appear here. An EMPTY array
is a real state — a patient-credit payment or an unallocated one — and it is not the same as the
payment having been deleted.

modifiedDateUtc.description:
Gets the change-feed watermark: `COALESCE(ModifiedUtcDate, CreatedUtcDate)`, in UTC.
    NON-NULLABLE by construction. The stored ModifiedUtcDate is nullable and is null for every
payment nobody has deleted, voided or re-shared — which is nearly all of them — so publishing that
column directly would make the ordinary population invisible to a consumer syncing on it. This field
carries the coalesced value and equals DateTimeOffset PublicPayment.CreatedUtcDate until the first edit. The query
parameter that filters on it is updatedSince; the asymmetry between the two names is deliberate
and platform-wide.

PublicPayment.description:
A payment. A HEADER ONLY — this is the first entity slice on the surface with no line collection at all.
    Property order is the wire order. The header drops InsuranceCompanyID, ToAccountID,
PaymentRequestID, RecurringPaymentId, PaymentDraftID, CreatedBy,
ModifiedByUserID, SharedWithPatient, TransactionReference (an internal trace id), the
computed PaymentReference and TransactionType, and the operator free text Notes,
VoidedReason and DeletedReason.
    NOTHING PROCESSOR-SIDE EXISTS ON THIS CONTRACT. No gateway transaction id, no processor name, no merchant
id, no terminal id, no token, no card metadata, no authorization code. CreditCardPayments is joined
for ONE column — the card brand in PublicCreditCardType? PublicPayment.CreditCardType — and the four other columns on that table
(CustomerVaultId, CardReference, NameOnCard, PaymentGatewayID,
SimpaySubType) are never read. PaymentInvoiceItems, PaymentDrafts,
RecurringPayments, SavedCreditCards and Accounts are never joined at all, and neither
are the patientCredits, tips, giftCardPayments, rewardsPayment and
refundHistory collections the internal payload carries.
    THERE IS NO isDeleted AND NO isVoided ON THIS PAYLOAD. Both stored flags fold into
PublicPaymentStatus PublicPayment.Status, with deletion taking precedence over voiding when a payment carries both.

id.description: Gets the payment mode id. This is the value a payment's `paymentModeId` refers to.

name.description: Gets the internal name. Practice-editable and not stable across tenants.

displayName.description:
Gets the name shown in the UI, or null when the practice never set one — in which case
`name` is what the UI falls back to. Practice-editable.

order.description: Gets the position the practice arranged this mode in, ascending.

paymentType.description:
Gets the payment method class. The only cross-tenant-stable way to bucket a payment mode: both
`name` and `id` are tenant-local, this is not.

isSystem.description:
Gets a value indicating whether this is one of the platform-seeded modes rather than one the practice
created.

isDeleted.description:
Gets a value indicating whether the mode has been removed by the practice. Deleted modes stay in this
lookup because historical payments still reference them; a consumer that only wants the currently
selectable modes filters on this field.

PublicPaymentMode.description:
A payment mode: the practice-configurable list a payment's `paymentModeId` points at.
    Property order is the wire order, and it is the field set PLA-1053 published — nothing more. The stored
row also carries ImageID, PaymentGatewayID and MerchantAccountID; those identify a
practice's payment processor and merchant account and are never exposed. The read path does not load
them, so this record cannot grow one by accident.

id.description:
Gets the payment mode id. TENANT-LOCAL — `PaymentModes.PaymentModeID` is an identity column in
each practice's own database, so the same number means different things in two tenants. Use it to join
against `/v1/financials/payment-modes` within one tenant, never to compare across them.

name.description:
Gets the mode's name. `NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL`, so `required` rather than nullable.
PRACTICE-RENAMABLE: it is what the practice typed, it can change under a consumer at any time, and two
practices' names for the same method rarely agree. Show it; do not group on it.

paymentType.description:
Gets the payment method class, and it is MANDATORY on this payload for a reason: it is the only
cross-tenant-stable way to bucket revenue by method. string PublicPaymentModeReference.Name is renamable and
int PublicPaymentModeReference.Id is tenant-local, so a consumer totalling collections by payment method across
practices has nothing else to group on.

PublicPaymentModeReference.description:
The payment method a payment was taken by, inline on the payment payload.
    A DISTINCT type from PublicPaymentMode, which /v1/financials/payment-modes returns. That
record publishes six fields — it adds displayName, order and isDeleted, which are
about how the practice ARRANGES its list of modes, not about the payment. Reusing it here would put three
fields on every payment that say nothing about that payment, and would make the lookup's field set
un-evolvable: adding a field there would silently widen this payload.
    The three fields here are the three a consumer needs to attribute the payment: the id to join on, the
label to show, and the type to bucket by.

id.description: Gets the payment reason id. This is the value a payment's `paymentReasonId` refers to.

description.description:
Gets the description. This is the column's name and the field name on the wire — the inline
reference object on `/v1/financials/payments` already publishes it as `description`, and the two must
agree.

isUseInsurance.description: Gets a value indicating whether the reason is used for insurance.

isSystem.description:
Gets a value indicating whether this is one of the platform-seeded reasons rather than one the
practice created.

isActive.description:
Gets a value indicating whether the reason is active. Inactive reasons stay in this lookup: the table
has no audit columns, so there is no other way for a consumer to notice a practice turned one off.

isDeleted.description:
Gets a value indicating whether the reason has been removed by the practice. Deleted reasons stay in
this lookup because historical payments still reference them; a consumer that only wants the
currently selectable reasons filters on this field.

PublicPaymentReason.description:
A payment reason: the practice-configurable list a payment's `paymentReasonId` points at.
    Property order is the wire order, and it is the field set PLA-1064 published — nothing more. The stored
row also carries DesignationID; Designations is out of the public surface entirely per
PLA-1053, and the read path does not load it, so this record cannot grow that field by accident.

id.description:
Gets the payment reason id. Tenant-local, and resolves against `/v1/financials/payment-reasons` — which
returns removed and inactive reasons too, precisely so a historical payment's reason stays resolvable.

description.description:
Gets the reason's label. `PaymentReasons.Description NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL`, so `required`
    rather than nullable — the whole object is null when the payment has no reason, so there is no state in
    which this is present and empty.
    A PRACTICE-CONFIGURED LOOKUP LABEL, not operator free text about this payment. It comes from a row in
PaymentReasons that the practice created once and reuses; it is not typed per payment and it
carries no patient detail. That is why the payment surface audits its reads with
carriedFreeText: false where the invoice, estimate and credit-note surfaces cannot.

isSystem.description:
Gets a value indicating whether this is one of the platform-seeded reasons rather than one the practice
created. Published because it is the only way to tell a reason whose meaning is fixed platform-wide —
and therefore comparable across tenants — from one a single practice invented.

PublicPaymentReasonReference.description:
The reason a payment was recorded under, inline on the payment payload.
    A DISTINCT type from PublicPaymentReason, which /v1/financials/payment-reasons returns, on
the same reasoning as PublicPaymentModeReference: that record adds
isUseInsurance, isActive and isDeleted, which describe the practice's CONFIGURATION
of the reason list rather than this payment.

PublicPaymentStatus.description:
Payment state. Fully derived from the internal deleted and voided flags, which are not exposed, so it
needs no Unknown sentinel: every input maps to exactly one of these three.

PublicPaymentType.description:
Payment method class. The only cross-tenant-stable way to bucket revenue: a payment mode's name is
tenant-renamable and its id is tenant-local.

PublicProviderSelectionType.description: How a provider is attached to a line or item. Its own zero value is the sentinel.

PublicServiceType.description: Catalog service classification. Its own zero value is the sentinel.

value.description:
Gets the value, exactly as it appears in an entity payload and exactly as the `status` filter
accepts it: the contract enum's declared PascalCase name, e.g. `PartiallyPaid`. The host
registers `JsonStringEnumConverter` with no naming policy, so enum VALUES are not camelCased
even though property NAMES are.

PublicStatus.description:
One status value: the wire string an entity's `status` field carries and its `status` filter
    accepts.
    One type serves all seven status lookups (PLA-1071). There is nothing per-status to carry — no id, no
tenant-local label, no ordering key — so seven identical single-field records would only put seven
interchangeable types in every generated client.

Bearer.description: Bearer access token. Send it as the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
